label: P-K-S
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{P-K-S}
Let a w.c.m.\, manifold $M^{2n+1}(\varphi_0,Q_0,\xi,\eta,g_0)$ with        
the
           
property \eqref{E-1k-0-nullity}
                                 
satisfy the condition \eqref{Eq-2assump}.
Then $(\varphi_0,Q_0,\xi,\eta,g_0)$ is a weak $K$-contact structure with $\mathcal{N}^{(5)}=0$, and there exists a smooth family $(\varphi_t,Q_{\,t},\xi,\eta,g_t)\ (t\in\mathbb{R})$
of weak $K$-contact structures on $M$ with  $\ker\eta$-adapted metrics $g_t$ (i.e., $g_t$ changes on $\ker\eta$~only) satisfying  \eqref{E-1k-0-nullity}, that converges exponentially fast, as $t\to-\infty$, to a Sasakian structure.

label: T-04
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{T-04}
Let a w.c.m. manifold
$M^{2n+1}(\varphi_0,Q_0,\xi,\eta,g_0)$ satisfy
\eqref{Eq-2assump} and
the $(\kappa,\mu)$-nullity condition \eqref{E-k-mu-nullity}.
Then $\kappa\le 1$, and

\smallskip
\noindent\
$(i)$ if $\kappa=1$, then the structure is  weak $K$-contact with $\mathcal{N}^{(5)}=0$,
and there exists a smooth family $(\varphi_t,Q_{\,t},\xi,\eta,g_t)\ (t\in\mathbb{R})$
                
of weak $K$-contact structures on $M$
with $\ker\eta$-adapted metrics $g_t$
satisfying  \eqref{E-1k-0-nullity}
                                
                                                  
that converges exponentially fast, as $t\to-\infty$, to a Sasakian structure.

\smallskip\noindent\
$(ii)$ if $\kappa<1$ and \eqref{E-nS-10} is true, then the eigenvalues of
$\widetilde h$, see \eqref{Eq-4.1}, are $\{\,0,\pm\sqrt{1-\kappa}\,\}$,
                                                    
                                    
$\ker\widetilde h=\{\xi\}$,
and the orthogonal decomposition
$\,\ker\eta={\cal D}_+\oplus{\cal D}_-$ is true, where ${\cal D}_\pm$ are $n$-dimensional
eigen-distributions of the eigenvalues $\pm\sqrt{1-\kappa}$, respectively, of $\widetilde h$, and the distributions ${\cal D}_\pm$ determine totally geodesic~foliations.
In~other words, ${\cal D}_+$ and ${\cal D}_-$ are conjugate Legendrian foliations.

label: thm6
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm6}
$(i)$ Let $M^{2n+1}(\varphi',\xi,\eta,g')$ be a contact metric manifold
and ${\lambda}>0$ be a differentiable function on~$M$. Then $(\varphi,Q,\xi,\eta,g)$ is a w.c.m. structure on $M$, where
\begin{align}\label{E-cont-lambda}
 \varphi ={\lambda}\,\varphi',\qquad
 g ={\lambda}^{-1}g'
 +(1-{\lambda}^{-1})\,\eta\otimes\eta,
 \qquad
 Q ={\lambda}^2 I + (1-{\lambda}^2)\,\eta\otimes\xi.
\end{align}
$(ii)$
Moreover, let
                                                                                                                                                    
              
${\lambda}>0$ be real, Then, $(\varphi,Q,\xi,\eta,g)$ satisfies the $(\kappa,\mu)$--nullity condition \eqref{E-k-mu-nullity}
if and only if $(\varphi',\xi,\eta,g')$ satisfies the $(\kappa',\mu')$-nullity condition
                         
with $\kappa'= {\lambda}^2(\kappa+3-{3\lambda})$ and $\mu'=\lambda(\mu+2-{2\lambda})$.

label: D-002
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{D-002}\rm
An $n$-dimensional distribution $D$ on a contact manifold $(M^{2n+1},\eta)$ is called a \textit{Legendrian distribution} if $d\eta(X,Y)=0$ for all vectors $X,Y$ in $D$. When the distribution $D$ is involutive, it defines a \textit{Legendrian foliation} on $(M^{2n+1},\eta)$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
Two Legendrian distributions $D$ and $D'$, or, foliations ${\cal F}$ and ${\cal F}'$,
of a w.c.m. manifold $M^{2n+1}(\varphi,Q,\xi,\eta,g)$
are said to be \textit{conjugate} if $\varphi(D')=D$,
or $\varphi(T{\cal F}')=T{\cal F}$, respectively,
and the tangent bundle splits as the orthogonal sum
$TM=D\oplus D'\oplus\{\xi\}$. Conjugate distributions or foliations form a pair known as a \textit{bi-Legendrian structure} on $M^{2n+1}$.

label: thm6.2
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{thm6.2}
For a w.c.m. structure $(\varphi,Q,\xi,\eta,g)$, we have
$d\eta(\varphi X, Y) = d\eta(\varphi Y, X)$ and
                                           
\begin{align}\label{3.1AA}
 2\,g((\nabla_{\xi}\,\varphi)X, Y)
                    
 = g([\xi,\varphi Y],\widetilde QX)
 -g([\xi,\varphi X],\widetilde QY)
 -\xi(g(\widetilde QX, \varphi Y)),
\end{align}
                                                                                        
in addition, the tensor $\mathcal{L}_{\xi}\,\varphi$
vanishes if and only if $\,\xi$ is a Killing vector field, i.e., $\mathcal{L}_{\xi}\,g=0$.

label: E-31
title: Proof
body_md:
On a w.c.m. manifold, the tensor $h$ and its conjugate $(1,1)$-tensor $h^*$ satisfy, see \cite{rov-119},
\begin{align}
\label{E-31}
 h-h^* & =  \nabla_{\xi}\,\varphi ,\\
 \label{E-31A}
 h\varphi+\varphi h &= -\tfrac12 \mathcal{L}_\xi\,Q
 ,\\
 \label{E-31B}
 h Q - Q h &= \tfrac12\,[\varphi, \mathcal{L}_\xi\,Q], \\
\label{E-30}
 Q\,\nabla \xi &= -\varphi(Q + h^*).
                                     
\end{align}
                                              
By conditions, \eqref{E-31A} and \eqref{E-31B}, $h$ anti-commutes with $\varphi$ and commutes with $Q$. The~same is true for $h^*$.
Since $Q$ is a self-adjoint positive definite (1,1)-tensor, the tensor $h$ is also self-adjoint, that is, $h=h^*$. Hence, \eqref{E-31} gives
$\nabla_{\xi}\,\varphi=0$.
By \eqref{E-30} and \eqref{P-6}, we have
               
 $\nabla \xi= - \varphi - \varphi\, Q^{-1} h^*$.
             
From this, $h=h^*$ we obtain \eqref{E-xi-n}.
Using \eqref{E-xi-n}, we get $\nabla_{\xi}\,{Q}=0$:
\begin{align*}
 0 = (\mathcal{L}_{\xi}\,{Q})X
 = [\xi, QX] - Q[\xi, X]
 = (\nabla_{\xi}\,{Q})X +Q\nabla_X\,\xi
 -\nabla_{QX}\,\xi
  = (\nabla_{\xi}\,{Q})X.
\end{align*}
If $h X=\lambda X$, then using $h\varphi = - \varphi h$
(by assumptions and \eqref{E-31A}),
we get $h \varphi X=-\lambda \varphi X$.
Thus, if $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $h$, then $-\lambda$ is also an eigenvalue of $h$; hence, ${\rm trace}\,h=0$.
By the above and Proposition~\ref{thm6.2},
a w.c.m. manifold is weak K-contact if and only if \eqref{E-xi-nK} is true.

label: Eq-nabla-phi-N5
title: Lemma
body_md:
For a w.c.m.\,structure, we have
\begin{align}\label{Eq-nabla-phi-N5}
 2\,g((\nabla_X \varphi )Y,Z) =g(\mathcal{N}^{(1)}(Y,Z),\varphi X)
 + 2\,g(\varphi X,\varphi Y)\,\eta(Z)
 -2\,g(\varphi X,\varphi Z)\,\eta(Y) +\mathcal{N}^{(5)}(X,Y,Z) ,
\end{align}
where
$\mathcal{N}^{(1)}:=N_\varphi+2\,d\eta\otimes\xi$, and the $(0,3)$-tensor ${\cal N}^{\,(5)}$ is given by
\begin{align*}              
\notag
 {\cal N}^{\,(5)}(X,Y,Z) =&\,\varphi Z(g(X, \widetilde QY))
 -\varphi Y(g(X, \widetilde QZ))
 -X(g(\varphi Z, \widetilde QY))
 +g([X, \varphi Z], \widetilde QY)\\
 & -\,g([X,\varphi Y], \widetilde QZ) +g([Y,\varphi Z] -[Z, \varphi Y] - \varphi[Y,Z],\ \widetilde Q X).
\end{align*}

title: Proof
body_md:
\eqref{E-1k-0-nullity} $\Rightarrow$
\eqref{E-nabla=phi-nullity}.
For $Y\perp\xi$ and $X=\xi$, \eqref{E-1k-0-nullity} reads $R_{\,\xi,Y}\,\xi = -QY$.
By this and \eqref{E-37}, we get $h^2 Y=0$. Since $h$ is a self-adjoint (1,1)-tensor, $h=0$ is true, and by Proposition~\ref{thm6.2}, $\xi$ is a Killing vector field.
Therefore, $(\varphi,Q,\xi,\eta,g)$
is a weak $K$-contact structure, and by \cite[Proposition~2]{rov-RS23}, we~get
\begin{align}\label{E-R-varphi}
 R_{\,\xi,X}=\nabla_X\,\varphi.
\end{align}
From \eqref{E-1k-0-nullity}, \eqref{E-R-varphi} and the first Bianchi identity, we obtain the equality
\[
 (\nabla_X\varphi)Y-(\nabla_Y\varphi)X
 =\eta(Y)\varphi^2X - \eta(X)\varphi^2\,Y .
                       
\]
By~\eqref{dPhi}, since $d{F}=0$, the equation above yields
\[
 g((\nabla_Z \varphi)Y, X) =
 g((\nabla_X \varphi)Y - (\nabla_Y \varphi)X, Z)
 =g( \eta(Y) \varphi^2X-\eta(X) \varphi^2\,Y, Z) ,
\]
which reduces~to \eqref{E-nabla=phi-nullity}.

\smallskip

\eqref{E-nabla=phi-nullity} $\Rightarrow$
\eqref{E-1k-0-nullity}.
The covariant derivative of $\varphi\,\xi=0$, using \eqref{E-xi-n},
\eqref{E-nabla=phi-nullity}, and the definition of $Q$, gives $\widetilde hX=0$, hence, $h = 0$. By Proposition~\ref{thm6.2}, $\xi$ is a Killing vector field,
and $(\varphi,Q,\xi,\eta,g)$
is a weak $K$-contact structure.
Therefore, we have \eqref{E-R-varphi}.
                                  
Applying this in conjunction with
\eqref{E-nabla=phi-nullity}, we have
\[
 R_{\,\xi,X}Y= \eta(Y)\varphi^2X -g(\varphi^2X,Y)\xi.
                                                  
 \]
From this, using the first Bianchi identity,
                                                                  
        
we get~\eqref{E-1k-0-nullity}.

Let \eqref{E-nabla=phi-nullity} be true. Then, $(\varphi,Q,\xi,\eta,g)$ is a weak $K$-contact structure. By Proposition~\ref{C-2cond}, \eqref{E-xi-n} holds with $h=0$.
              
Taking the covariant derivative of $Q=-{\varphi}^2 + {\eta}\otimes {\xi}$ and using \eqref{E-nabla=phi-nullity} along with $\nabla\xi =-\varphi$, we~get,
\begin{align*}
 (\nabla_X Q)Y &= -(\nabla_X \varphi^2)Y + [g(\nabla_X \xi,Y)\xi+ \eta(Y)\nabla_X \xi] \\
 &  = -(\nabla_X \varphi)(\varphi Y)- f(\nabla_X \varphi)Y - g(\varphi X,Y) \xi - \eta(Y)\varphi X \\
 & =\eta(Y)Q\varphi X+g(QY,\varphi X)\xi  - g(\varphi X,Y) \xi - \eta(Y)\varphi X,
 \end{align*}
which is equivalent to \eqref{E-nS-10K}.

label: T-PRF-g2b
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{T-PRF-g2b}
Let $M^{2n+1}(\varphi_0,Q_{\,0},\xi,\eta,g_0)$ be a weak $K$-contact manifold.
Then, there exist $\ker\eta$-adapted Riemannian metrics $g_t\ (t\in\mathbb{R})$
-- a solution of
        
\eqref{E-GF-Rmix-Phi} -- such that each $(\varphi_t,Q_{\,t},\xi,\eta,g_t)$ is a weak $K$-contact structure on $M$ with structural tensors defined on 
${\ker\eta}$ as
\begin{equation}\label{E-Q-phi}
 Q_{\,t}|_{\ker\eta}=R_{\xi,t}\,,
 \quad
 \varphi_t\,|_{\,{\ker\eta}}=T_{\xi}^\sharp(t) ,
\end{equation}
where the operator ${T}^{\sharp}_\xi:{\ker\eta}\to{\ker\eta}$ is defined by
   
$g({T}^{\sharp}_\xi X,Y)=
         
\tfrac12\,\eta([X,Y])$.
Moreover,~$g_t$  converges exponentially fast, as $t\to-\infty$, to a limit metric $\hat g$
with $\widehat R_\xi={I}_{\ker\eta}$ that provides an $K$-contact structure $(\hat \varphi,\xi,\eta,\hat g)$
on $M$.

label: L-PRF-2
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
In our case, $\overset{\centerdot} g(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Ric}_{\ker\eta}(X,Y) +2\,g^\top(X,Y)$.
Since $Q|_{\ker\eta}= {I}_{\ker\eta} +\widetilde Q$, where $\widetilde Q = Q-I$, by \eqref{E-Q-phi}, we have
                                    
 $\nabla_Y R_\xi =
 \nabla_Y \widetilde Q + \nabla_Y {I}_{\ker\eta}$.
               
Using this, $\nabla_Z\,\widetilde Q=\nabla_Z\,Q$ and \eqref{E-GF-Rmix-Phi}, we obtain
\begin{align*}
 (\nabla_Z\,\overset{\centerdot} g)(X,Y) = -2\,g((\nabla_Z\, R_\xi)X, Y)
 +2\,g((\nabla_Z\,{I}_{\ker\eta})X, Y) = -2\,g((\nabla_Z\,Q)X,Y).
\end{align*}
We also have, see \cite[Section~5.3.7.2]{Rov-Wa-2021},
                          
\begin{align}\label{E-PRF-fT}
 \overset{\centerdot}{T}\,^{\sharp}_\xi =
 2\,(R_\xi - {I}_{\ker\eta}) {T}^{\sharp}_\xi .
\end{align}
In view of \eqref{E-PRF-fT} and \eqref{E-Q-phi}, we have
               
 $\overset{\centerdot}\xi = \overset{\centerdot}\eta = 0$
 and
 $\overset{\centerdot} \varphi = \overset{\centerdot} T\,\!_{\xi}^\sharp
 = 2\,(R_\xi - {I}_{\ker\eta}) {T}^{\sharp}_{\xi}$.
             
Using \eqref{E-PRF-fK}, \eqref{E-Q-phi} and
$\overset{\centerdot} R_\xi = \overset{\centerdot} Q + \overset{\centerdot}{I}_{\ker\eta}=\overset{\centerdot} Q$,
we also have
               
$ \overset{\centerdot}{\varphi^2} = -\overset{\centerdot} Q = -4\,R_\xi(R_\xi -\,{I}_{\ker\eta})$.
             

Let's calculate the evolution under PRF of the equality \eqref{E-nabla=phi-nullity}. We have
\begin{align} \label{Eq-ev}
 (\overset{\centerdot}\nabla_X\,\varphi)Y
 +(\nabla_X\,\overset{\centerdot} \varphi)Y
 =\eta(Y)\overset{\centerdot}{\varphi^2}X
 -g(\overset{\centerdot}{\varphi^2}\,Y,X)\xi
 -\overset{\centerdot} g(\varphi^2Y,X)\xi .
\end{align}
      
Recall the general formula, e.g., \cite[Eq.~(4.8)]{Rov-Wa-2021},
                                  
\begin{equation}\label{eq2G}
 2\,g(\overset{\centerdot}\nabla_X Y, Z) = (\nabla_X\,\overset{\centerdot} g)(Y,Z)
 +(\nabla_Y\,\overset{\centerdot} g)(X,Z)-(\nabla_Z\,\overset{\centerdot} g)(X,Y).
                                 
\end{equation}
By the above, symmetry of the covariant derivative of $Q$, \eqref{E-nS-10K}
(see Proposition \ref{L-cond-equiv})
and \eqref{eq2G},
                                 
we have
\begin{align*}                     
\notag
 g((\overset{\centerdot}\nabla_X\,\varphi)Y,Z)  &=
 g(\overset{\centerdot}\nabla_X(\varphi Y),Z) + g(\overset{\centerdot}\nabla_X Y,\varphi Z)\\
 & = \tfrac12\{(\nabla_X\,\overset{\centerdot} g)(\varphi Y,Z)
 + (\nabla_{\varphi Y}\,\overset{\centerdot} g)(X,Z) -(\nabla_Z\,\overset{\centerdot} g)(X,\varphi Y)
 \notag\\
 & \quad +(\nabla_X\,\overset{\centerdot} g)(Y,\varphi Z)
 +(\nabla_Y\,\overset{\centerdot} g)(X,\varphi Z)
 -(\nabla_{\varphi Z}\,\overset{\centerdot} g)(X,Y)\} \notag\\
 & = -\{g((\nabla_X Q)\varphi Y,Z)
 +g((\nabla_{\varphi Y} Q)X,Z)
 -g((\nabla_Z Q)X,\varphi Y) \notag \\
 &\quad
 +g((\nabla_X Q)Y, \varphi Z) + g((\nabla_Y Q)X,\varphi Z)
 -g((\nabla_{\varphi Z} Q)X,Y)\} \notag\\
 & =-2\,\eta(Y) g(\widetilde Q \varphi X, \varphi Z), \\
                                
 g( (\nabla_X\,\overset{\centerdot}\varphi )Y, Z)& = g(\nabla_X (\overset{\centerdot} \varphi Y),Z) -g(\overset{\centerdot} \varphi \nabla_X Y,Z) \notag \\
 & = 2\,g((\nabla_X Q)\varphi Y,Z)
 + 2\,g((R_\xi - {I}_{\ker\eta})
 (\nabla_X \varphi)Y,Z) \notag \\
&  = 2\,\eta(Z) g(\widetilde Q\varphi X, \varphi Y)
+ 2\, \eta(Y) g((R_\xi
- {I}_{\ker\eta})\varphi ^2X,Z) \notag \\
& = 2\,\eta(Z) g(\widetilde Q\varphi X, \varphi Y)
- 2\,\eta(Y) g(\widetilde Q\varphi  X,\varphi Z).
\end{align*}
Therefore, the inner product of the LHS of \eqref{Eq-ev} with $Z$
                                 
is as follows:
\begin{align}\label{E-PRF-cond1a}
 g( (\overset{\centerdot}\nabla_X\,\varphi)Y
 +(\nabla_X\,\overset{\centerdot}\varphi)Y, Z) =
 -4\,\eta(Y) g(\widetilde Q X, QZ)
 +2\,\eta(Z) g(\widetilde QX, QY).
\end{align}
Similarly, using $I_{\ker\eta}\,\widetilde Q=\widetilde Q$, \eqref{E-nS-10K} and \eqref{E-Q-phi}, for all $X,Y,Z\in\mathfrak{X}_M$ we calculate
\begin{align*}
                     
 \eta(Y)g(\overset{\centerdot}{\varphi ^2}X,Z) &=-4\, \eta(Y) \, g(R_\xi(R_\xi -\,{I}_{\ker\eta})X,Z)
                              
 =-4\,\eta(Y) g(\widetilde Q X, QZ), \\
  
 -\eta(Z)g(\overset{\centerdot}{\varphi ^2}Y,X)
 &=4\,\eta(Z)g(R_\xi(R_\xi-{I}_{\ker\eta})Y,X)
 = 4\,\eta(Z)g(Q^2Y - QY,X)
       
 = 4\,\eta(Z)g(\widetilde QY,QX), \\
   
                       
 -\eta(Z)\overset{\centerdot} g(\varphi ^2Y,X) &=
 2\,\eta(Z)\{g(R_\xi\,\varphi ^2 Y,X)
 -g^\top(\varphi^2Y,X)\}
 = 2\,\eta(Z)\{g(Q\varphi^2 Y,X)
 - g(\varphi^2Y, X)\}  \\
 & = - 2\,\eta(Z) g(\widetilde Q\varphi X, \varphi Y) = - 2\,\eta(Z) g(\widetilde QX, QY) .
\end{align*}
Therefore, the inner product of the RHS of \eqref{Eq-ev} with $Z$
                                 
is as follows:
\begin{align}\label{E-PRF-cond1b}
g(\eta(Y)\overset{\centerdot}{\varphi ^2}X -g(\overset{\centerdot}{\varphi ^2}\,Y,X)\xi
 -\overset{\centerdot} g(\varphi ^2Y,X)\xi,\ Z) =
 -4\,\eta(Y) g(\widetilde Q X, QZ)
 +2\,\eta(Z) g(\widetilde QX, QY).
\end{align}
Since the RHS of \eqref{E-PRF-cond1a} and \eqref{E-PRF-cond1b}
coincide, \eqref{Eq-ev} holds.
Thus, \eqref{E-nabla=phi-nullity} is preserved under the PRF~\eqref{E-GF-Rmix-Phi}.

label: 4.NN
title: Proof
body_md:
By Proposition \ref{L-cond-equiv}, \eqref{E-1k-0-nullity} and \eqref{E-nabla=phi-nullity} are equivalent; moreover, $M$ carries a weak $K$-contact structure.
Using the Levi-Civita connection $\nabla$ of $g$, one can rewrite the tensor $N_\varphi$ as
               
\begin{align}\label{4.NN}
 N_\varphi(X,Y) = ({\varphi}\nabla_Y{\varphi}
 -\nabla_{{\varphi} Y}{\varphi}) X
 -({\varphi}\nabla_X{\varphi}
 -\nabla_{{\varphi} X}{\varphi}) Y .
\end{align}
From
                
\eqref{4.NN} and \eqref{E-nabla=phi-nullity},
we~have
\begin{align*}
 g(\mathcal{N}^{(1)}(Y,Z),\varphi X)
 = g(\varphi (\nabla_Z \varphi) Y
 -(\nabla_{\varphi Z}\varphi ) Y
 -\varphi (\nabla_Y \varphi)Z
 +(\nabla_{\varphi Y}\varphi) Z,\ \varphi X)
                                                                                                                                                     
 =0.
\end{align*}
Applying this in conjunction with
                 
\eqref{E-nabla=phi-nullity} (see Proposition~\ref{L-cond-equiv}), we reduce \eqref{Eq-nabla-phi-N5} to the equality
${\cal N}^{\,(5)}=0$.

By Theorem~\ref{T-PRF-g2b} and Proposition~\ref{L-PRF-2}, there exists an $\ker\eta$-adapted family $(\varphi_t,Q_{\,t},\xi,\eta,g_t)$ of weak K-contact structures on $M$,
which converges exponentially fast, as $t\to-\infty$, to a limit K-contact structure
$(\hat\varphi,\xi,\eta,\hat g)$ satisfying~\eqref{E-1k-0-nullity}
and \eqref{E-nabla=phi-nullity}.
By well-known results, e.g., \cite[Proposition~7.6]{blair2010riemannian}, the structure
$(\hat\varphi,\xi,\eta,\hat g)$ is Sasakian.

title: Example
body_md:
\rm
To illustrate Theorem~\ref{P-K-S},
we consider a
                     
w.c.m.~manifold
$M^{2n+1}(\varphi_0,Q_0,\xi,\eta,g_0)$
with $Q_0 =\lambda\,I$ on $\ker\eta$ for some real positive $\lambda\ne1$,
satisfying the condition  \eqref{E-1k-0-nullity}.
                                 
By Theorem~\ref{T-PRF-g2b} in Section~\ref{sec:02.2},
and the theorem of uniqueness of a solution to ODE \eqref{E-PRF-fK}, we have a $\ker\eta$-conformal solution $R_{\xi,t}
=\mu(t)\,I_{\ker\eta}$.
                     
Set $g^\top(X,Y)=g(X^\top,Y^\top)$.
                                                              
Since $\overset{\centerdot} I_{\ker\eta}=0$, we have the ODE $\overset{\centerdot}\mu=4\mu\,(\mu-1)$ with $\mu(0)=\lambda>0$.
Thus, $\mu(t)=\frac{1}{1-C\,e^{4t}}\ (t\in\mathbb{R})$, where $C=1-\lambda^{-1}\ne0$.
Since our PRF \eqref{E-GF-Rmix-Phi} reduces to ODE, applying the theorem of uniqueness of a solution to ODE, we~have
                           
$g\,\!^\top_t=\rho(t)\,g\,\!^\top_0$, where
$\rho(0)=1$ and
\begin{align*}
 &\overset{\centerdot} g\,\!^\top_t =-2\mu(t)g^\top_t
 +2\,g^\top_t = 2\,(1-\mu(t))\,g^\top_t
 \implies \frac{d}{dt}\log \rho(t)=2\,(1-\mu(t))
 =  -\frac{2\,Ce^{4t}}{1-C e^{4t}} .
    
                          
                                                      
                                          
                
                                                    
 \end{align*}
Thus, $g_t$ is conformal on $\ker\eta$ with the conformal factor equal to
$\rho(t)= \big(\frac{1-C e^{4t}} {1-C}\big)^{1/2}$.
By~the above,
\[
 \varphi_t=\varphi_0/\rho(t),\quad Q_{\,t}|_{\ker\eta}=\frac{1}{1-Ce^{4t}}\,I_{\ker\eta},\quad
     
 g_t=
         
\eta\otimes\eta +\rho(t)\,g^\top_0.
\]
                                                                   
By Theorem~\ref{P-K-S},
$(\varphi_t,Q_{\,t},\xi,\eta,g)$ $(t\in\mathbb{R})$,
is a~smooth family of weak $K$-contact structures on $M$ satisfying
\eqref{E-1k-0-nullity}, that converges exponentially fast, as $t\to-\infty$, to a Sasakian structure
$(\lambda^{-1/2}\varphi_0, \xi,\eta,\,
         
\eta\otimes\eta+\lambda^{1/2}g^\top_0)$.

title: Proof
body_md:
By Proposition~\ref{prop-5.1}(i), the eigenvalues of $\widetilde{h}$ are $\{0, \pm\sqrt{1-\kappa}\}$ and $\kappa\le1$.

            

$(i)$ Let $\kappa=1$, then $\widetilde{h}=h=0$.
Therefore, \eqref{E-k-mu-nullity} reduces to~\eqref{E-1k-0-nullity}.
By Proposition~\ref{C-2cond}, \eqref{E-xi-n} reduces to $\nabla\,{\xi}=-\varphi$,
                                                                                                 
           
and $(\varphi,Q,\xi,\eta,g)$ is a weak $K$-contact structure.
                                                                     
By Theorem~\ref{P-K-S}, there exists an $\ker\eta$-adapted fami\-ly $(\varphi_t,Q_{\,t},\xi,\eta,g_t)$ of weak K-contact structures on $M$,
which converges exponentially fast, as $t\to-\infty$, to a limit Sasakian structure
$(\hat\varphi,\xi,\eta,\hat g)$.
                                                

\smallskip

$(ii)$ Let $\kappa<1$.
By Proposition~\ref{prop-5.1}(ii), the contact distribution $\ker\eta$ decomposes into a direct sum
of mutually orthogonal eigen-distributions
${\cal D}_+$ and ${\cal D}_-$,
corresponding to the eigenvalues $\sqrt{1-\kappa}$ and $-\sqrt{1-\kappa}$ of $\tilde h$, respectively.
Let $X,Y\in{\cal D}_+$, or, ${\cal D}_-$, then using \eqref{E-xi-n} we get
               
 $g(\nabla_X\,\xi,Y)= -(1\pm\sqrt{1-\kappa})\,g(\varphi X,Y) = 0$.
             
Thus, $0=2\,g(QX,\varphi Y)= 2\,d\eta(X,Y)=- \eta([X,Y])$.
By~\eqref{E-k-mu-nullity}, $R_{X,Y}\,\xi=0$ for $X,Y \in\ker\eta$.
Using this for $X,Y,Z\in{\cal D}_+$, or, $X,Y,Z\in{\cal D}_-$, respectively, we have
\begin{align*}                 
 \notag
 0&
 = g(R_{X,Y}\,\xi,Z)
                           
           
                            
                            
         
     
 = -(1\pm\sqrt{1-\kappa})\,(\nabla_Z{F})(X,Y)
 \mp 2\sqrt{1-\kappa}\,g(\varphi [X,Y],Z).
\end{align*}
Applying \eqref{Eq-phi02} and \eqref{Eq-phi001} (where \eqref{E-nS-10} is used) in the above relation yields
$g(\varphi [X,Y],Z)=0$. Using this and $\eta([X,Y])=0$, we get $[X,Y]\in {\cal D}_+$, or, $[X,Y]\in {\cal D}_-$\,, respectively, which shows that the distributions ${\cal D}_+$ and ${\cal D}_-$ are involutive.

Fix $X,Z\in{\cal D}_-$ and $Y\in {\cal D}_+$, then using the fact $R_{e_1,e_2}\,\xi=0\ (e_1, e_2 \in\ker\eta)$, we have
                  
\begin{align*}
 0&= g(R_{X,Y}\,\xi ,Z) =
 (1+\sqrt{1-\kappa})\big\{ (\nabla_X {F})(Y,Z)
 + (\nabla_Y {F})(Z,X)\big\}
 - 2\,\sqrt{1-\kappa}\, g(\varphi \nabla_Y X,Z), \\
 & = (1+\sqrt{1-\kappa}) (\nabla_Z {F})(X,Y)- 2\,\sqrt{1-\kappa}\, g(\varphi \nabla_Y X,Z).
\end{align*}
Using \eqref{Eq-phi02}, gives
$(\nabla_Z {F})(X,Y)=0$, which implies $g(\nabla_Y X,\varphi Z)=0$ for $X,Z\in{\cal D}_+$ and $Y\in{\cal D}_-$.
Hence, $\nabla_Y X\
(X\in{\cal D}_+,\,Y\in{\cal D}_-)$
is orthogonal to ${\cal D}_-$.
   
Ta\-king  \(Y,Z\in{\cal D}_+\) and \(X\in{\cal D}_-\), and applying \eqref{E-xi-n}, gives
   
$g(\nabla_Y Z, \xi) = -g(\nabla_Y \xi, Z) = (1+ \sqrt{1-\kappa})g(\varphi Y, Z) = 0$
       
and
                   
$g(\nabla_Y Z, X) = -g(Z, \nabla_Y X) = 0$.
   
By~ the above, \(\nabla_Y Z \perp {\cal D}_- \oplus  \{\xi\}\), hence
\({\cal D}_+\) is totally geodesic. Applying the same procedure for $X,Z\in{\cal D}_+$ and $Y\in {\cal D}_-$ and using \eqref{Eq-phi02}, we conclude that ${\cal D}_-$ is totally geodesic.

title: Proof
body_md:
$(i)$ This follows from the conditions and Definition~\ref{D-02}.

$(ii)$  Note that $g'(X,\xi)=\eta(\xi)=g(X,\xi)$ and
$g'(X,Y^\top)={\lambda}\,g(X,Y^\top)$, where $Y^\top$ is the $\ker\eta$-component of $Y$.
Let $\nabla'$ and $\nabla$ be the Levi-Civita connections of the metrics $g'$ and $g$, respectively.
In the Koszul formula for $g'$,  we expand each term using
$g'(X,Y) = {\lambda}\,g(X,Y) + (1-{\lambda})\,\eta(X)\eta(Y)$, see \eqref{E-cont-lambda}, to obtain
\begin{align*}
 & 2\,g'(\nabla'_X Y, Z)
                              
                                                        
                        
                                            
                                                  
                                                 
                                                                                       
                                                 
                           
                                                               
                                                 
                                                      
                                   
 = 2\,{\lambda}\,g(\nabla_X Y,Z)
 +2(1{-}{\lambda})\,\eta(\nabla_X Y) \eta(Z)
 +(1{-}{\lambda})\big\{(\nabla_X \eta)(Y)\eta(Z)  \\
 &+\eta(Y)(\nabla_X \eta)(Z)
 +(\nabla_Y\eta)(X)\eta(Z) +\eta(X)(\nabla_Y \eta)(Z) -(\nabla_Z \eta)(X)\eta(Y)-\eta(X)(\nabla_Z \eta)(Y)\big\}.
\end{align*}
Simplifying the above by using
                            
the relation $(\nabla_X\,\eta)(Y)= g(\nabla_X\,\xi,Y) =-g(\varphi X +\varphi\,\widetilde h X,Y)$ and the fact $g'(\nabla_X Y,Z) = {\lambda}\,g(\nabla_X Y,Z)
 +(1-{\lambda})\,\eta(\nabla_X Y) \eta(Z) $, we have
\begin{align*}
 & 2\,g'(\nabla'_X Y, Z) = 2\,g'(\nabla_X Y, Z) +(1-{\lambda})\big\{-\eta(Z) g(\varphi X +\varphi\,\widetilde h X,Y)
 -\eta(Y) g(\varphi X +\varphi\,\widetilde h X,Z) \\
 & -\eta(Z) g(\varphi Y {+}\varphi\,\widetilde h Y,X) {-}\eta(X)\,g(\varphi Y {+}\varphi\,\widetilde h Y, Z)
 {+}\eta(Y)\,g(\varphi Z {+}\varphi\,\widetilde h Z,X) {+}\eta(X)\,g(\varphi Z {+}\varphi\,\widetilde h Z,Y) \big\}.
\end{align*}
With further simplification, we obtain
\begin{align}\label{E-nabla'}
 \nabla'_X Y =\nabla_XY+ (1-{\lambda})\,\big\{g(\widetilde hX,\varphi Y)\xi-\eta(Y) \varphi X-\eta(X) \varphi Y\big\}.
\end{align}
 From \eqref{E-k-mu-nullity} and the definition of $Q$, we have
$ R_{\,\xi,X}Y = \kappa\{ g(QX,Y)\xi
- \eta(Y)QX \}
 + \mu \{ g(hX,Y)\xi - \eta(Y)hX \}.$
Using the previous equation and \eqref{E-05b} gives
\begin{equation*}
(\nabla_{hX}\varphi)Y
= {\lambda}^4(1-\kappa )\big[ g(X,Y)\xi-\eta(Y)X \big]
+ {\lambda}^2\big[\eta(Y)hX - g(hX,Y)\xi\big].
\end{equation*}
Next, in the above equation, we substitute $hX$ in place of $X$ and use the equality
 $h^2X =(1-\kappa)\big\{Q^2X -\eta(X) \xi\big\},$
see the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop-5.1}, to obtain
\begin{equation}\label{Eq-varphi}
 (\nabla_X \varphi)Y = {\lambda}^2[g(X,Y)\xi-\eta(Y) X] +g(hX,Y)\xi-\eta(Y) hX.
\end{equation}
We set
 $A(X,Y) := g(\widetilde hX,\varphi Y)\xi - \eta(Y)\varphi X - \eta(X)\varphi Y$,
and using this along with \eqref{E-nabla'},  find
             
                                                                                                                       
\[
 R'_{X,Y}\,\xi = R_{X,Y}\,\xi
 +(1-{\lambda})\big\{(\nabla_X A)(Y,\xi)
 -(\nabla_Y A)(X,\xi) +A(X,A(Y,\xi)) -A(Y,A(X,\xi)) \big\}.
\]
By \eqref{Eq-varphi}, we have the following expressions:
\begin{align*}
 (\nabla_X A)(Y,\xi) =& -2g(hX,Y)\xi -(2-\kappa) {\lambda}^2 g(X,Y)\xi
 +[(1-\kappa){\lambda}^2+1]\eta(X)\eta(Y)\xi\\
 & +2{\lambda}^2\eta(Y)X +2\eta(Y) hX ,\\
  
 A(X, A(Y,\xi)) =& -A(X, \varphi Y) = -g( hX, Y)\,\xi+\eta(X)\varphi^2 Y.
\end{align*}
Using these two equations and the definition of $\varphi'$,
$h = \tfrac12\mathcal{L}_{\xi}\,\varphi = {\lambda}\,\tfrac12\mathcal{L}_{\xi}\,\varphi'= {\lambda}\,h'$, and \eqref{E-k-mu-nullity}, we have
\begin{align*}
 R'_{X,Y}\,\xi &= R_{X,Y}\,\xi + (1-{\lambda}) \big\{3(\eta(X) \varphi^2Y-\eta(Y) \varphi^2X ) + 2(\eta(Y) hX -\eta(X) hY)\big\} \\
 & ={\lambda}^2(\kappa+3(1-{\lambda}))\big\{ \eta(X)\varphi'^2Y -\eta(Y)\varphi'^2X \big\}
 + {\lambda}(\mu+ 2(1-{\lambda}))\,\big\{ \eta(Y) h'X -\eta(X) h'Y\big\} .
\end{align*}
Taking $\kappa'= \lambda^2(\kappa+3(1-\lambda))$ and $\mu' =\lambda(\mu+2(1-\lambda))$, we see that $(\varphi',\xi,\eta,g')$ is a $(\kappa',\mu')$-structure.

title: Proof
body_md:
By \eqref{E-nS-10} and Example~\ref{Ea-dim3}$(ii)$, $Q|_{\ker\eta}={\lambda}^2\,I_{\,\ker\eta}$ for some real ${\lambda}>0$.
By Theorem~\ref{thm6},
                                                       
$(\varphi',\xi,\eta,g')$ is a contact metric structure with
$\varphi'={\lambda}^{-1}\varphi$ and
$g'={\lambda} g+(1-{\lambda})\eta\otimes\eta$,
                                                
satisfying the $(\kappa',\mu')$-nullity condition with
$\kappa'= \kappa+3{\lambda}^2(1-{\lambda})$ and
$\mu'=\mu+2{\lambda}(1-{\lambda})$.
Applying \cite[Theorem~3]{blair1994}
                                                       
we conclude that $M^3(\varphi',\xi,\eta,g')$ is locally isometric to any of the following unimodular Lie groups $G$ with a left-invariant~metric:

$SU(2)$ or $SO(3)$, when $c_2>0$ and $c_3>0$;

$SL(2,\mathbb{R})$, or, $O(1,2)$, when $c_2<0$, and $c_3>0$, or, $c_2<0$ and $c_3<0$;

$E(2)$, when $c_2=0$ and $\mu<2$, including a flat structure when $\mu=0$;
    

$E(1,1)$, when $c_3=0$ and $\mu>2$;
          
where
$c_2 = 1-\sqrt{1-\kappa}-\tfrac12\,\mu$
and
$c_3=1+\sqrt{1-\kappa}-\tfrac12\,\mu$.

\noindent
Here, $G$ is the Lie group with a 3-dimensional Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$,
having a basis $\{E_1,E_2,\xi\}$, and the following Lie brackets:
               
 $[E_1,E_2]= 2\,{\lambda}\,\xi$,
 $[E_2,\xi]=c_2 E_1$, and
 $[\xi,E_1]=c_3 E_2$,
             
where ${\lambda}>0,c_2,c_3$ are real
and $\mu = 2-(c_2+c_3)$.

                                                                                                             
                            

                                                                                                                           
   
                                                                                                                      
                     
                                    
   
Define an almost w.c.m. structure $(\varphi, Q,\xi,\eta,g)$ on $G$ as~follows:
\begin{align*}
 &\varphi E_1= {\lambda} E_2, \quad \varphi E_2=-{\lambda} E_1, \quad \varphi\,\xi=0,
 \quad QE_1 ={\lambda}^2 E_1, \quad QE_2 ={\lambda}^2 E_2, \quad Q\,\xi=\xi,
\end{align*}
$g$ is the left-invariant Riemannian metric such that $\{E_1,E_2,\xi\}$ is an orthonormal frame and $\eta$ is the dual $1$-form of $\xi$ with respect to $g$.
                                                                                                      
                                                   
Note that the images of $E_1,E_2$ under $\widetilde h$ are
$
  \widetilde hE_1= \tfrac1{2{\lambda}}\,(c_3-c_2)\,E_1, \, \widetilde hE_2=-\tfrac1{2{\lambda}}\,(c_3-c_2)\,E_2,
 $
indicating ${\cal D}_+$ is spanned by $E_1$ and ${\cal D}_-$ by $E_2$.
                                
 
The following relations are satisfied:
\begin{align*}
 &\nabla_{E_1} E_2 =\tfrac{1}{2}(2{\lambda}-c_2+c_3)\,{\xi},\quad
 \nabla_{E_1}\,\xi= \tfrac{1}{2}(c_2-c_3-2{\lambda})\,E_2, \quad
 \nabla_{E_2}\,\xi =\tfrac{1}{2}(2{\lambda}+c_2-c_3)\,E_1, \\
 & \nabla_{\xi} E_1 = \tfrac{1}{2}(c_2+c_3-2{\lambda})E_2, \quad
 \nabla_{\xi} E_2 = \tfrac{1}{2}(2{\lambda}-c_2-c_3)E_1, \quad \nabla_{E_1} E_1 = \nabla_{E_2}E_2 =\nabla_{\xi}\,\xi = 0.
\end{align*}
Using the above relations, we find the following components of the curvature tensor:
\begin{align*}
& R_{\,E_1, \, E_2}\,\xi=0, \quad
 R_{\,E_1,\, \xi}\,\xi=-\big\{1-\tfrac1{4{\lambda}^2}\,(c_3-c_2)^2\big\}\,\varphi^2 E_1 + \tfrac{1}{{\lambda}}(2{\lambda}- {c_2} - {c_3})\,hE_1, \\
&R_{\,E_2,\, \xi}\,\xi= -\big\{1-\tfrac1{4{\lambda}^2}(c_3-c_2)^2\big\} \varphi^2 E_2 + \tfrac{1}{{\lambda}}(2{\lambda}-{c_2} -{c_3})\,hE_2.
\end{align*}
                
Choosing
                     
   
 $\kappa= 1-\tfrac1{4{\lambda}^2}(c_3-c_2)^2
 \le 1$
 and
        
$\mu=\tfrac{1}{\lambda}(2{\lambda}-c_2-c_3)$,
we get
  
   
the $(\kappa,\mu)$-nullity condition on $G$.
                              
                                                                                                      
                
                                                    
                                                                                      
                                                       
                                                      
              
       
                          
                                                
Moreover, \eqref{Eq-2assump} and \eqref{E-nS-10} are valid.
                                                                                                                                 
Since $\kappa<1$ for $c_2\ne c_3$, we have the desired~structure.

title: Example
body_md:
\rm
We illustrate Theorem~\ref{T-04}$(ii)$  by representing a w.c.m. manifold satisfying the conditions \eqref{E-k-mu-nullity}
with $\kappa<1$, \eqref{Eq-2assump} and \eqref{E-nS-10}.
For $n=1$, this also illustrates Corollary~\ref{Thm-lie} since the manifold is locally isomorphic to $E(1,1)$.
Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a $(2n+1)$-dimensional Lie algebra with a basis $\{E_1,\ldots,E_n,{\cal E}_1,\ldots,{\cal E}_n,\xi\}$
and the Lie bracket (satisfying the Jacobi identity) defined as follows for a real ${\lambda}>0$ (for ${\lambda}=1$, see
\cite{CMdiT-2007}):
                                            
                                                                                     
\begin{align}\label{E-Lie_ex4}
\notag
 &[E_a,E_b]=0 \quad \text{for any } a,b\in\{1,\ldots,n\},
 \qquad [{\cal E}_a,{\cal E}_b]=0 \quad \text{for any } a\ne 2,\\
\notag
 &[{\cal E}_2,{\cal E}_b]=2\,{\lambda}\,{\cal E}_b\  \text{ for any } b\ne 2, \quad [E_1,{\cal E}_1]=2\,{\lambda}\,({\xi}-E_2), \quad [E_1,{\cal E}_b]=0\  \text{ for any } b\ge 2,\\
\notag
 &[E_a,{\cal E}_b]=2\,{\lambda}\,\delta_{ab}({\xi}-E_2) \quad \text{for any } a,b\ge 3,
\qquad [E_2,{\cal E}_b]=2\,{\lambda}\,E_b \text{ for any } b\ne 2,\\
\notag
 &[E_2,{\cal E}_2]=2\,{\lambda}\,{\xi}, \qquad
 [E_a,{\cal E}_1]=[E_a,{\cal E}_2]=0\ \text{ for } a\ge 3, \\
 &[\xi,E_b]=0, \qquad
 [\xi,{\cal E}_b]=2\,{\lambda}\,E_b
\quad \text{for any } b\in\{1,\ldots,n\}.
\end{align}
                                                                                                                         
Define a weak almost contact structure
\((\varphi,Q,\xi,\eta)\)
on a Lie group $G$ of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ by
            
\begin{align}\label{E-f_ex4}
       
 \varphi\,E_a={\lambda} {\cal E}_a, \quad
 \varphi\,{\cal E}_a=-{\lambda} E_a
 \quad (1\le a\le n),
 \quad \varphi\,\xi=0,
 \quad
 Q=\lambda^2 I+(1-\lambda^2)\,\eta\otimes\xi,
 \quad
 \eta=\xi^\flat.
    
                                                                                               
\end{align}
                                                                                                              
Let $g$ be a left-invariant Riemannian metric on $G$ such that $\{E_1,\ldots,E_n,\,{\cal E}_1,\ldots,{\cal E}_n,\,\xi\}$ is an orthonormal frame.
Then $(\varphi,Q,\xi,\eta,g)$ satisfies \eqref{Eq-2assump} and \eqref{E-nS-10}.
                                           
Note that $n$-dimensional distributions ${\cal D}_+=Span\{E_1,\ldots,E_n\}$ and
 ${\cal D}_-=Span\{{\cal E}_1,\ldots,{\cal E}_n\}$ are
 involutive.

Using \eqref{E-Lie_ex4} and \eqref{E-f_ex4}, we have
the following non-zero derivatives of the frame:
\begin{align}\label{E-nabla_ex4}
\notag
&
                               
                               
\nabla_{E_1}\xi=-2\,{\lambda}\, {\cal E}_1, \quad                                
                          
            
\nabla_{E_2}\xi=-2\,{\lambda}\,{\cal E}_2, \quad
                               
                               
\nabla_{E_a}{\cal E}_b=2\,{\lambda}\delta_{ab}\,{\xi}, \\
       
&\nabla_{E_a}\xi=-2{\lambda}\,{\cal E}_a, \quad
\nabla_{{\cal E}_1}{\cal E}_1=2\,{\lambda}\,{\cal E}_2,\quad
                                
                                      
                                       
     
                                
                                      
\nabla_{{\cal E}_a}{\cal E}_2=-2{\lambda}\,{\cal E}_a,\quad
\nabla_{{\cal E}_a}{\cal E}_b=2{\lambda}\delta_{ab}\,{\cal E}_2,
      
                          
\end{align}
for all $a,b\in\{3,\ldots,n\}$, from which we find the non-zero components of the curvature tensor:
\begin{align*}
                                
                                                                           
                                                                
                                
                                                                
                         
                                                                                            
                                
& R_{E_1,\xi}\,\xi = 4{\lambda}^2 E_1, \ \quad
  R_{E_2,\xi}\,\xi = 4{\lambda}^2 E_2, \quad
  R_{E_a,\xi}\,\xi = 4{\lambda}^2 E_a, \\
& R_{{\cal E}_1,\xi}\,\xi = -4{\lambda}^2 {\cal E}_1, \quad
  R_{{\cal E}_2,\xi}\,\xi = -4{\lambda}^2 {\cal E}_2, \quad
  R_{{\cal E}_a,\xi}\,\xi = -4{\lambda}^2 {\cal E}_a.
\end{align*}
We also have $\widetilde h(E_a)=E_a$ and
$\widetilde h({\cal E}_a)=-{\cal E}_a$ for $a\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$.
              
                                                                 
                                                    
Let us show that $d\eta(X,Y) =g(X,\varphi Y)$
is true for the orthonormal basis
$\{E_a, {\cal{E}}_a, \xi\}_{1 \le a \le n}$.
Obviously, $d \eta(X,Y)=0=g(X, \varphi Y)$ holds for $X=\xi$ or
$Y=\xi$. Using \eqref{E-Lie_ex4}, for $X,Y\in\ker\eta$, we have
$d\eta(E_a, E_b) =d\eta({\cal E}_a, {\cal E}_b)=0\ (1\le a,b\le n)$
and $d\eta(E_a, {\cal{E}}_b) = \lambda\,\delta_{ab}$.
               
                                 
                                         
                                       
                                                        
                                                            
                                          
                                
                   
                            
             

Also, using the orthonormality of $\{E_1,\ldots,E_n,{\cal E}_1,\ldots,{\cal E}_n,\xi\}$ and the definition of $\varphi$, we have
\begin{align*}
    g(E_a, \varphi E_b)= g({\cal E}_a, \varphi  {\cal E}_b) =0, \quad g(E_a, \varphi {\cal E}_b) = -\lambda \, \delta_{ab}.
\end{align*}
Therefore, $(\varphi,Q,\xi,\eta,g)$ is a w.c.m. structure on $G$
satisfying the condition
\eqref{E-k-mu-nullity} with $\kappa=0$ and $\mu=4$.
 Moreover, ${\cal D}_+$ and  ${\cal D}_-$ are conjugate Legendrian foliations, which together with $\xi$ form a web of totally geodesic foliations.
              
                                             
    
                                                            

This manifold does not split along the
                 
distributions
${\cal D}_+$, ${\cal D}_- $, and $\{\xi\}$.
                                                                                                                                                          
 Indeed,
                           
                                                                                   
                 
        
${\cal D}_- \oplus \{\xi\}$
                                   
is not closed under the Lie bracket~\eqref{E-Lie_ex4}; moreover, by \eqref{E-nabla_ex4},
                                                                             
${\cal D}_+ \oplus \{\xi\}$ fails to be totally geodesic.

title: Proof
body_md:
It was shown in Theorem~\ref{T-04}$(ii)$ that ${\cal D}_\pm$ are totally geodesic distributions.
For $X\in{\mathcal D}^-$, $\nabla_{[\xi,X]}\,\xi=-R_{\,\xi,X}\,\xi=0$; thus, $\widetilde h\,[\xi,X]=-[\xi,X]$, i.e., $[\xi,X]\in{\mathcal D}^-$. Combining this with the involutivity of ${\mathcal D}^-$, we find that ${\mathcal D}^-\oplus\{\xi\}$ is involutive.
  
Consider a foliated chart $U$ with coordinates $x_1,\ldots,x_{2n+1}$ such that $\{\partial_j\}_{j>n}$ is a local basis of ${\mathcal D}^-\oplus\{\xi\}$.
There exist smooth functions $c^j_a$ on $U$, $a\in\{1,\dots ,n\}$ and $ j\in \{n+1,\dots,2n+1\}$ such that
$X_a=\partial_a+\sum_{j>n}c^j_a \partial_j$
is a basis of ${\mathcal D}^+$.
Since $[\partial_j, X_a]\in{\mathcal D}^-\oplus\{\xi\}$ for $j>n$ and $a\le n$, we can write
$[\partial_j, X_a]=X+\sigma\,\xi$, where $X\in{\mathcal D}^-$ and $\sigma\in C^\infty(U)$.
                             
               
By~$\nabla_{[\partial_j, X_a]}\,\xi = \nabla_X\,\xi   + \sigma\nabla_{\xi}\,\xi = 0$,
             
                 
$\xi$ is parallel along
$[\partial_j, X_a]$.
Then, using \eqref{E-RXY-xi} and~\eqref{E-xi-n},
\begin{align*}
 0 =R_{\,\partial_j, X_b}\, \xi =
  \nabla_{\partial_j}\nabla_{X_b}\,\xi
 -\nabla_{X_b}\nabla_{\partial_j}\,\xi
 -\nabla_{[\partial_j, X_b]}\,\xi
 = -2\,\nabla_{\partial_j}(\varphi X_b),
\end{align*}
                                                     
and $\nabla_{\varphi X_a}(\varphi X_b)=0$,
since $\varphi X_a\in{\mathcal D}^-$.
Thus, ${\mathcal D}^-\oplus\{\xi\}$ determines a flat, totally geodesic foliation.
Let's show that the distributions ${\cal D}_+$ and ${\cal D}_-\oplus [\xi]$ are parallel.
By \eqref{E-xi-n} for $X,Z\in {\mathcal D}^-$ and  $Y\in {\mathcal D}^+$, we find
\begin{align*}                 
 g(R_{X,Y}\,\xi, Z) &= g(\varphi \widetilde{h}\nabla_X Y,Z)- g(\varphi \widetilde{h}\nabla_Y X,Z)
 -2g((\nabla_X \varphi )Y,Z) -g(\varphi \nabla_X Y,Z) -g(\varphi \nabla_Y X,Z)  \notag \\
 & = 2 (\nabla_X {F})(Y,Z)-2g(\varphi \nabla_Y X,Z).
\end{align*}
This yields the equality
$(\nabla_X{F})(Y,Z)=g(\varphi\nabla_Y X,Z)$.
From \eqref{Eq-phi03} (where \eqref{E-nS-10} is used), we find \(g(\nabla_Y X, \varphi Z) = 0\) for $X,Z\in {\mathcal D}^-$ and  $Y\in {\mathcal D}^+$. Since \(\varphi\) is an isomorphism from \({\cal D}_-\) onto \({\cal D}_+\), this implies that \(\nabla_Y X\) is orthogonal to \({\cal D}_+\), thus,
\(\nabla_Y X\) lies in ${\cal D}_- \oplus \{\xi\}\), indicating the distribution is parallel.
Using the total geodesy of ${\cal D}_- \oplus \{\xi\}$, we have $g(\nabla_YX, Z) =-g(X, \nabla_Y Z)=0$ for $X\in{\mathcal D}^+$ and $Y,Z\in{\cal D}_-$, indicating ${\cal D}_+$ is a parallel distribution.
By the de Rham Decomposition Theorem and the fact that \({\cal D}_- \oplus \{\xi\}\) determines a flat totally geodesic foliation, \(M\) splits with one of the factors locally isometric to $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$.
By Theorem~\ref{T-04}(ii), $({\cal D}_+,{\cal D}_-)$ is a bi-Legendrian structure.

\smallskip

In the rest of the proof, all calculations are done for $X,Y,Z,W\in{\cal D}_+$.
                                                             
Using \eqref{E-xi-n}, we have
\[
 g((\nabla_X\,\varphi)Y,\xi)= -g((\nabla_X\,\varphi )\xi,Y)
 = g(\varphi\nabla_X\,\xi, Y) = 2\,g(\varphi X,\varphi Y)
 = 2\,g(QX,Y),
\]
hence, from \eqref{Eq-phi02}, we acquire
\begin{align}\label{E-phi2}
 (\nabla_X\,\varphi)Y=2\,g(QX,Y)\xi .
                             
\end{align}
Since ${\cal D}_+$ is totally geodesic, we have $\nabla_W Z\in{\cal D}_+$.
Using this and \eqref{E-phi2}, we~get
\begin{align}\label{E-RXY1}
\notag
 & g(\nabla_X \nabla_Y \varphi Z,\varphi W)-g(\nabla_X \nabla_Y Z, W)
 = g(\nabla_X (2g(QY,Z)\xi +\varphi\nabla_Y Z),\varphi W)  \\
                                                                                                                    
 &-g(\nabla_X \nabla_Y Z, W) = -4\,g(QY,Z)g(QX,W) +g(\nabla_X\nabla_Y Z, \widetilde QW) .
\end{align}
From \eqref{E-phi2} we have the following:
\begin{align}\label{E-RXY2}
\notag
 g(\nabla_{[X,Y]}\,\varphi Z, \varphi W)
 {-}g(\nabla_{[X,Y]} Z,W)
             
 &=2\,g(Q[X,Y],Z)\,g(\xi,\varphi W) {+} g(\varphi\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z,\varphi W) {-}g(\nabla_{[X,Y]} Z,W) \\
 &=g(\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z, Q W) -g(\nabla_{[X,Y]} Z,W)
  = g(\nabla_{[X,Y]} Z,\widetilde QW).
\end{align}
Comparing \eqref{E-RXY1} with \eqref{E-RXY2}
and using $Q=I+\widetilde Q$, we get
\begin{align*}
 g(R_{X,Y}\varphi Z,\varphi W) - g(R_{X,Y}\,Z, QW)
 = 4\, g(QX,Z)\,g(Y,QW) - 4\, g(X,QW)\,g(QY,Z) .
                               
\end{align*}
As the manifold splits as a product of manifolds,                                 
$g(R_{X,Y} \varphi Z, \varphi W)=0$ for $X,Y,Z,W \in {\cal D}_+$, indicating that after replacing $QW$ by $W$, we have
\begin{align}\label{E-RXY3}
    g(R_{X,Y}\,Z,W) = 4\,\{g(QY,Z)\,g(X,W) -g(QX,Z)\,g(Y,W)\} \qquad
 (X,Y,Z,W\in{\cal D}_+).
\end{align}
Next, using the skew-symmetry of the Riemannian curvature tensor, we have
\[
 0=g(R_{X,Y}\,Z,Z)= 4\,\{g(QY,Z)\,g(X,Z) -g(QX,Z)\,g(Y,Z)\}.
\]
Taking $Z\in\mathcal{D}_+$ as a unit vector and setting $X=Z$ yields
\begin{align*}
    g(QY,Z)=g(QZ,Z)\,g(Y,Z)\qquad (Y\in\mathcal D_+).
\end{align*}
By symmetry of $Q$, we have
   
$QZ = g(QZ,Z)\,Z$.
   
Thus, every nonzero vector in $\mathcal{D}_+$ is an eigenvector of $Q$.
                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
   
                                       
   
                                                                                                          
                
Hence, $Q|_{\mathcal{D}_+} =\lambda\, I|_{\mathcal{D}_+}$ for some smooth function $\lambda$ on $M$. Since $\varphi$ and $Q$ commute and $\varphi (\mathcal{D}_-)=\mathcal{D}_+$, for $V \in \mathcal{D}_ -$ we have
\[
\varphi QX =Q\varphi V = \lambda\, \varphi V \implies \varphi (QV -\lambda \, V)=0.
\]
Since, $\varphi$ is injective on $\ker\eta$, it follows that $QV =\lambda \, V$. From this and above, $Q|_{\ker\eta} =\lambda\, I|_{\ker\eta}$.
The~conditions \eqref{Eq-2assump} and \eqref{E-nS-10} force $\lambda $ to be a positive real constant. Consequently, \eqref{E-RXY3} simplifies~as
\[
g(R_{X,Y}\,Z,W) = 4\lambda\,\{g(Y,Z)\,g(X,W) -g(X,Z)\,g(Y,W)\} \qquad
 (X,Y,Z,W\in{\cal D}_+).
\]
Hence, the integral manifolds of $\mathcal{D}_+$ have constant sectional curvature $1/\sqrt{4\lambda}$ and the manifold is locally isometric to $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\times \mathbb{S}^n(4\lambda)$.

Suppose, on the contrary, that a w.c.m. manifold of dimension $\ge 5$ is flat.
                               
                     
Since the manifold satisfies \eqref{E-RXY-xi}
along with \eqref{Eq-2assump} and \eqref{E-nS-10},
the equation~\eqref{E-RXY3} is valid
                                                 
and reduces to
               
\begin{align}\label{E-cor1}
 g(Y,Z)\,g(X,W) = g(Y,W)\,g(X,Z) \quad (X,Y,Z,W\in {\cal D}_+).
\end{align}
Choose $Z=Y$ and $W=X$, then 
              
\eqref{E-cor1} yields
   
$g(X,Y)^2= g(X,X)\,g(Y,Y)$.
   
By the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, this equality holds if and only if $X$ and $Y$ are linearly dependent. This contradicts our assumption
$\dim{\cal D}_+=n\ge 2$, that is, $X$ and $Y$ can be chosen to be linearly independent.

\rm \label{Ea-dim3}
$(i)$
                                                 
Let $M^{2n+1}(\varphi,Q,\xi,\eta,g)$  be a w.c.m. manifold with the curvature-related property \eqref{E-RXY-xi}, and
the tensor $Q|_{\,\ker\eta}$ be a scalar multiple of the identity map, i.e., $Q|_{\ker\eta}=\lambda\,I_{\,\ker\eta}$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}_{+}$. Then, the conditions \eqref{Eq-2assump} and \eqref{E-nS-10} are true, and Theorem~\ref{T-04b} can be applied. By \eqref{E-RXY3},
the integral manifolds of ${\cal D}_+$ have constant sectional curvature $4\lambda>0$,
and the manifold is locally isometric to
$\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\times\mathbb{S}^{n}(4\lambda)$.



$(ii)$ For $\dim M=3$, we illustrate Theorem~\ref{T-04b} with an example with fewer assumptions, which agrees with the result
of \cite[Section~7.5]{blair2010riemannian}.
Let a w.c.m. manifold \( M^3(\varphi, Q, \xi, \eta, g) \) satisfy conditions \eqref{E-RXY-xi} and \eqref{E-nS-10}.
Then $Q|_{\ker\eta}={\lambda}^2 I|_{\ker\eta}$ for some real $\lambda>0$,
see Example~\ref{Ea-dim3}$(ii)$.
Hence, the condition \eqref{Eq-2assump} is true. By Theorem~\ref{T-04b}, our manifold is locally isometric to $\mathbb{R}^2\times\mathbb{R}$; hence, the metric $g$ is flat. We~have the following Lie bracket relations:
\[
 [e_2,\xi]= 0,\quad
 [\xi, e_1]=2\,{\lambda}\,e_2,\quad
 [e_1,e_2]=2\,{\lambda}\,\xi,
\]
which determine locally the Lie group $E(2)$ with a left-invariant metric.
                                                      
The~following equations are true:
 $\nabla_{e_1}\xi =-2\,{\lambda}\,e_2, \ \nabla_{e_2}\,\xi = 0$, and $\nabla_{\xi}\,\xi=0$.
Thus, $\xi$ rotates along the ${\cal D}_-$-curves with the speed equal to $2\,{\lambda}$.

label: E-39
title: Proof
body_md:
Using \eqref{E-nabla-phi-Phi}, \eqref{E-xi-n} and \eqref{E-nS-10b}, we have
\begin{align}
 (\nabla_X {F})(\varphi Y,Z)  - (\nabla_X {F})( Y,\varphi Z)
 & = -\, \eta(Y)g((Q+h)X,\varphi Z)
 -\eta(Z)g((Q+h)X,\varphi Y) \label{E-39}.
\end{align}
Replacing $Z$ by $\varphi Z$ in \eqref{E-39}, we acquire
\begin{align}
 (\nabla_X {F})(\varphi Y, \varphi Z) - (\nabla_X {F})(Y,\varphi^2 Z)
 = \eta(Y)[g((Q+h)X,QZ) -\eta(X) \eta(Z)].
 \label{E-40}
\end{align}
 A simple computation gives
 $(\nabla_X {F})( Y,\varphi^2 Z) =
 -(\nabla_X {F})(Y, QZ)
 -\eta(Z)[g((Q+h)X,Y)-\eta(X)\eta(Y)].$
Inserting this in \eqref{E-40}, gives
\begin{align}\label{E-41}
  
(\nabla_X {F})(\varphi Y, \varphi Z)
+ (\nabla_X {F})(Y, QZ)
= \eta(Y)g((Q+h)X,QZ) -\eta(Z)g((Q+h)X,Y) .
                                       
\end{align}
Using \eqref{dPhi}, we get
\begin{align*}
 &\quad (\nabla_X {F})(Y,Z)+ (\nabla_Y {F})(Z,X)+(\nabla_Z {F})(X,Y) +(\nabla_{\varphi X} {F})(\varphi Y,Z)+(\nabla_{\varphi Y}{F})(Z,\varphi X) \\
 & \quad+(\nabla_Z {F})(\varphi X, \varphi Y)
 +(\nabla_{\varphi X}{F})(Y, \varphi Z)
 +(\nabla_Y{F})(\varphi Z, \varphi X)
 +(\nabla_{\varphi Z}{F})(\varphi X,Y)\\
 & \quad -(\nabla_X {F})(\varphi Y, \varphi Z)
 -(\nabla_{\varphi Y} {F})(\varphi Z, X)-(\nabla_{ \varphi Z} {F})(X, \varphi Y) =0.
\end{align*}
Applying \eqref{E-39} and \eqref{E-41}, the above equality simplifies to
\begin{align} \label{E-41a}
 &2(\nabla_X {F})(Z,Y)+ 2 (\nabla_{\varphi X} {F})(Z,\varphi Y)  = 4\,{\eta}(Z) g(QX,QY)
 -[2\eta(Y)g((Q+h)X,QZ)\notag \\
 &+2\eta(X)\eta(Y) {\eta}(Z) -\eta(Y)g((Q+h)Z, \widetilde Q X)\notag
 +\eta(Z)g((Q+h)Y, \widetilde Q X)\\
 &-\eta(X)g((Q+h)Z, \widetilde Q Y)]
 +(\nabla_X {F})(Y,\widetilde QZ)-(\nabla_Y {F})(Z,\widetilde QX)-(\nabla_Z {F})(X,\widetilde QY).
\end{align}
Observe that using \eqref{E-nS-10}, and then the anti-symmetry of $\varphi$ and the equality $\nabla Q=\nabla \widetilde Q$, we have
\begin{align} \label{E-Phi}
 (\nabla_X {F})(Y,\widetilde QZ)=
 (\nabla_X {F})(\widetilde QY,Z)
 +\eta(Z)g((Q+h)X,\widetilde QY) +\eta(Y)g((Q+h)X,\widetilde QZ)
\end{align}
for all $X,Y,Z \in\mathfrak{X}_M$.
By the above and $d{F}=0$, the equation \eqref{E-41a} simplifies as
 \begin{align*}                     
 \notag
 & (\nabla_X {F})(Z,Y) + (\nabla_{\varphi X} {F})(Z,\varphi Y) =  2\,{\eta}(Z) g(QX,QY) - \big[\eta(Y)g((Q+h)X,QZ) \\
  & +\eta(X)\eta(Y) {\eta}(Z) +\tfrac12\,\eta(Z)\,g((Q+h)Y,\widetilde Q X)\big]
  +\tfrac12\big[(\nabla_X {F})(Y,\widetilde QZ)
  +(\nabla_{\widetilde Q X} {F})(Y,Z) \big] ,
 \end{align*}
that is equivalent to \eqref{E-04}.

label: E-42
title: Proof
body_md:
Using \eqref{E-xi-n},
proved based on the condition \eqref{Eq-2assump},
we find
                                                
\begin{align} \label{E-42}
 R_{Y,Z}\,\xi = -(\nabla_Y\,\varphi)Z
 + (\nabla_Z\,\varphi)Y
 - (\nabla_Y\,\varphi\widetilde h)Z
 + (\nabla_Z\,\varphi\widetilde h)Y.
\end{align}
                                                                    
Taking the scalar product of \eqref{E-42} with $X$ and simplifying using \eqref{dPhi}, we get the relation
              
                                                                            
\begin{align}\label{E-05}
 g(R_{\xi,X}Y ,Z)=-(\nabla_X {F})(Y,Z)-g(X,(\nabla_Y\,\varphi\widetilde h)Z)+ g(X, (\nabla_Z\,\varphi  \widetilde h)Y).
\end{align}
Using \eqref{E-05}, we have the following:
\begin{align}\label{E-42-tilde}
 g(R_{\xi,X}Y, Z) &-g(R_{\xi, X}\varphi Y, \varphi Z)
 + g(R_{\xi,\varphi X}Y, \varphi Z)
 +g(R_{\xi,\varphi X}\varphi Y, Z) \notag \\
 &= A(X,Y,Z) + \widetilde B(X,Y,Z) - \widetilde B(X,Z,Y) ,
\end{align}
where the operators $A$ and $\widetilde B$ are defined as follows:
\begin{align*}
 & A(X,Y,Z) = -(\nabla_X {F})(Y,Z) +(\nabla_X {F})(\varphi Y,\varphi Z) -(\nabla_{\varphi X} {F})(Y, \varphi Z)  -(\nabla_{\varphi X} {F})(\varphi Y,Z), \\
 & \widetilde B(X,Y,Z) = g(X, (\nabla_{\varphi Y}\varphi\widetilde h)\varphi Z) - g(X, (\nabla_Y\varphi\widetilde h)Z)
  - g(\varphi X, (\nabla_Y\varphi\widetilde h)\varphi Z) - g(\varphi X, (\nabla_{\varphi Y}\varphi\widetilde h)Z).
\end{align*}
Using \eqref{E-04}, \eqref{E-39}, \eqref{E-41} and \eqref{E-Phi}, the operator $A$ is simplified as
                           
                                                  
                                   
            
\begin{align}\label{eq-a1}
\notag
A(X,Y,Z) =& \,\big\{
 (\nabla_X {F})(Y,Z)+(\nabla_{X} {F})(fY,fZ)\big\}
+\big\{(\nabla_{fX} {F})(fY,Z)
-(\nabla_{fX} {F})(Y, fZ)\big\} \\
       
 =&\,2\,\eta(Z) g(QX, QY)
 -2\,\eta(Y) g(QX, QZ)
  +(\nabla_{\widetilde Q X} {F})(Y,Z) ,
\end{align}
and the operator $\widetilde B$ is read as
\begin{align*}
 &\widetilde B(X,Y,Z)
 = g(X, \varphi(\nabla_Y\,\widetilde Q\widetilde h)Z)
 -g( X,(\nabla_{Y}\,\varphi)\widetilde hZ)
+g(X, (\nabla_{\varphi Y}\,Q\widetilde h) Z)
+g(X,\widetilde h\varphi(\nabla_{\varphi Y}\,\varphi)Z) \\
&+g( X, \varphi(\nabla_{\varphi Y}\,\varphi) \widetilde h Z)
+g(Q X, \widetilde h(\nabla_Y\,\varphi) Z)
-g(Q X, (\nabla_{\varphi Y}\,\widetilde h) Z)
 +\eta(X)\,\eta((\nabla_{\varphi Y}\,\widetilde h) Z).
\end{align*}
 Using \eqref{E-nS-10} and \eqref{E-xi-n}, we get
                                                                                                                                                            
\begin{align*}
 & g(X, (\nabla_{\varphi Y}\,Q \widetilde h) Z)
 = g(X, Q(\nabla_{\varphi Y}\,\widetilde h) Z)
 -\eta(X)g((Q-h)Y,\widetilde Q \widetilde hZ), \\
   
 & g(\varphi X, (\nabla_Y \widetilde Q \widetilde h)Z) = g(\varphi X, \widetilde Q( \nabla_Y \widetilde h)Z).
\end{align*}
These two equations allow us to simplify
                   
$\widetilde B(X,Y,Z)$ as follows:
\begin{align*}
 &\widetilde B(X,Y,Z)
 =-g(X,(\nabla_{Y}\varphi)\widetilde hZ) -g(\widetilde Q \varphi X, (\nabla_Y\,\widetilde h)Z) +g(X, \widetilde h \varphi (\nabla_{\varphi Y}\,\varphi) Z) \\
 &\quad
 +g(Q X, \widetilde h(\nabla_Y \varphi) Z) +g(X,\varphi(\nabla_{\varphi Y}\,\varphi)\widetilde h Z) - \eta(X)g((Q{-}h)Y,\widetilde QhZ)
 +\eta(X)\,\eta((\nabla_{\varphi Y}\,\widetilde h) Z).
\end{align*}
In order to simplify $\widetilde B(X,Y,Z)$, we compute $\varphi(\nabla_{\varphi Y} \varphi)Z$ using \eqref{2.2}, \eqref{E-xi-n}, \eqref{E-04} and \eqref{E-nS-10b} as follows:
\begin{align}\label{e-phi}
 \varphi (\nabla_{\varphi Y} \varphi)Z
 & =(\nabla_{\varphi Y}\varphi^2)Z
 -(\nabla_{\varphi Y} \varphi)\varphi Z
 \notag \\
 & = -\big(g(QY,QZ)-\eta(Y)\eta(Z)\big){\xi} +2\,{\eta}(Z)\big(Q^2Y-\eta(Y)\xi\big)
 \notag \\
 & \quad -g(hY,QZ)\xi
 +(\nabla_Y\,\varphi)Z + P(Y,Z)
 +\tfrac{1}{2}\,g((Q+h)Z,\widetilde QY)\xi ,
\end{align}
where
                                   
$P(X,Y):=\frac{1}{2}\big[
\widetilde Q (\nabla_X\,\varphi)Y
 +(\nabla_{\widetilde QX}\,\varphi)Y \big]$.
Using
$\eta((\nabla_{\varphi Y} \widetilde h)Z)
=-g(\widetilde hZ, \nabla_{\varphi Y}\xi)
=g(Q\widetilde hZ, \widetilde hY-Y)$
and \eqref{e-phi},
we further simplify $\widetilde B(X,Y,Z)$ to
\begin{align}\label{Eq-b1}
\notag
 &\widetilde B(X,Y,Z) = 2\,g(\widetilde hX, (\nabla_{Y}\varphi) Z)
 +2\,{\eta}(Z)g( hX, QY) -2\,{\eta}(X)g(QY, hZ)+g(\widetilde{Q}X, \varphi (\nabla_Y \widetilde h)Z)  \\ & \quad
 +g(\widetilde{Q}X, \widetilde h(\nabla_{Y}\varphi) Z)
 +g(\widetilde h P(Y,Z)+P(Y, \widetilde hZ), X)
  + \tfrac{1}{2}\eta(X) g((Q+h)Y,\widetilde QZ)  .
                                              
\end{align}
                                                                       
We rewrite \eqref{E-42-tilde} using $d{F}=0$, \eqref{E-Phi}, \eqref{eq-a1}, and \eqref{Eq-b1} as follows:
\begin{align}\label{E-ABB}
 & A(X,Y,Z) + \widetilde B(X,Y,Z) - \widetilde B(X,Z,Y) \notag\\
 & \quad = 2\,(\nabla_{\widetilde hX}{F})(Y,Z)
 +2\,{\eta}(Z)g((Q+h)X,QY) -2\,{\eta}(Y)g((Q+h)X,QZ) \notag \\
 & \quad
                                                    
 + (\nabla_{\widetilde QX} {F})(Y,Z) \notag + (\nabla_{\widetilde Q \widetilde hX} {F})(Y,Z)
 - g(\varphi\widetilde QX,\ (\nabla_Y\widetilde h)Z -(\nabla_Z\widetilde h)Y) \notag \\
 & \quad
 +g(\widetilde h P(Y,Z)+P(Y,\widetilde hZ), X)
 -g(\widetilde h P(Z,Y)+P(Z, \widetilde hY), X).
\end{align}
Using $d{F}=0$ and \eqref{E-Phi}, we simplify the last four terms in \eqref{E-ABB}:
                                                 
\begin{align*}
2\,g(\widetilde h P(Y,Z)&+P(Y,\widetilde hZ), X)  -2\,g(\widetilde h P(Z,Y)+P(Z,\widetilde hY), X) \\
  & = (\nabla_{\widetilde Q \widetilde h X} {F})(Y,Z)
 + (\nabla_Y {F})(\widetilde QX,\widetilde hZ)
 -(\nabla_Z {F})(\widetilde QX,\widetilde hY)
 -(\nabla_{\widetilde QY} {F})(Z,\widetilde hX)
 \\
 & \quad  -(\nabla_{\widetilde QY} {F})(\widetilde hZ,X) +(\nabla_{\widetilde QZ} {F})(Y,\widetilde hX)
  +(\nabla_{\widetilde QZ}{F})(\widetilde hY,X).
\end{align*}
      
From \eqref{E-05} we have
\begin{align*}
 & g(\widetilde Q X, \varphi(\nabla_Z\widetilde h)Y -\varphi(\nabla_Y\widetilde h)Z)
      
 = g(\widetilde Q X, (\nabla_Z\,\varphi\widetilde h)Y -(\nabla_Y\,\varphi\widetilde h)Z)
 -g(\widetilde Q X, (\nabla_Z\,\varphi)\widetilde h Y -(\nabla_Y\,\varphi)\widetilde h Z) \\
  
 & = g(R_{\xi,\widetilde Q X}Y, Z)
 + (\nabla_{\widetilde QX} {F})(Y,Z)
 -(\nabla_Z{F})(\widetilde Q X,\widetilde h Y)
 +(\nabla_Y{F})(\widetilde Q X,\widetilde h Z).
 \end{align*}
Finally, using the two expressions above, we simplify \eqref{E-ABB} to the following:
\begin{align} \label{E-CURV}
 &A(X,Y,Z) + \widetilde B(X,Y,Z) - \widetilde B(X,Z,Y)\notag \\
 \notag
  =&\,2\,(\nabla_{\widetilde hX} {F})(Y,Z)
 +2\,{\eta}(Z)g((Q+h)X,QY) -2\,{\eta}(Y)g((Q+h)X,QZ) \notag \\
 \notag
                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                               
 &+ \tfrac{1}{2}\big[ 3(\nabla_{\widetilde Q\widetilde hX}{F})(Y,Z)
 -(\nabla_{\widetilde QY}{F})(Z,\widetilde hX)
 -(\nabla_{\widetilde QY}{F})(\widetilde h Z, X) +(\nabla_Y {F})(\widetilde hZ, \widetilde QX)\\
 &+ (\nabla_Z {F})(\widetilde QX,\widetilde hY)
 -(\nabla_{\widetilde QZ}{F})(X,\widetilde hY) -(\nabla_{\widetilde QZ}{F})(\widetilde hX,Y) \big]
 -g(R_{\xi,\widetilde Q X}Y, Z).
\end{align}
The required equality \eqref{E-05b} follows from \eqref{E-CURV}.

\(M^{2n+1}(\varphi,Q,\xi,\eta,g)\) satisfy conditions
\eqref{E-k-mu-nullity} and \eqref{Eq-2assump}.

\quad (X,Z\in{\mathcal D}^-,\ Y\in {\mathcal D}^+),\\

label: E-31a
title: Proof
body_md:
$(i)$ From the $(\kappa,\mu)$-nullity condition
\eqref{E-k-mu-nullity}, we get
 $QR_{\,\xi, X}\, \xi=\kappa\,Q\varphi^2X-\mu\, QhX$
 and  $\varphi R_{\,\xi,\,\varphi X}\,\xi =
-\kappa\,Q\,\varphi^2 X -\mu\,QhX$.
Combining these two equations, we acquire
\begin{align}\label{E-31a}
 QR_{\,\xi, X}\,\xi
 -\varphi R_{\,\xi,\,\varphi X}\,\xi
 = 2\kappa\,Q\varphi^2 X.
\end{align}
Comparing \eqref{E-31a} with \eqref{E-37}
where \eqref{Eq-2assump} is used, we get
$h^2X =(1-\kappa)\big\{Q^2X -\eta(X) \xi\big\}$,
hence
                             
$\widetilde h^{\,2}X=(1-\kappa)X\ (X\in\ker\eta)$.
             

Since $\widetilde h=Q^{-1}h$ is self-adjoint,
$\widetilde h^{\,2}$ is non-negative definite; hence
$\kappa\le 1$ holds. Since $\widetilde{h}\,\xi=0$ is true, we have $\ker\widetilde h=\{\xi\}$ and $\ker\eta={\cal D}_+ \oplus {\cal D}_-$,
where ${\cal D}_\pm+$ are the eigen-distributions for the eigenvalues $\pm\sqrt{1-\kappa}$.
                        
                
Using $\varphi h = -h \varphi$ and $\varphi Q = Q \varphi$, we obtain
$\widetilde{h}(\varphi X)=-\sqrt{1-\kappa}\,\varphi X\ (X\in{\cal D}_+)$, which ensures
$\varphi X\in{\cal D}_-$. Thus, $\varphi$ maps ${\cal D}_+$ onto ${\cal D}_-$ and vice versa, so $\dim {\cal D}_+ = \dim {\cal D}_- = n$. Observe that $g(\varphi X, \varphi Y)=0$ for $X \in {\cal D}_+$ and $Y \in {\cal D}_-$, which gives $g(QX,Y)=0$. Thus,
$Q({\cal D}_+)={\cal D}_+$ and $Q({\cal D}_-)={\cal D}_-$,
similarly, $\widetilde Q({\cal D}_+)={\cal D}_+$ and $\widetilde Q({\cal D}_-)={\cal D}_-$.
                                            

\smallskip

$(ii)$ From \eqref{E-05b} (where \eqref{E-nS-10} is used) with $X,Y,Z\in\ker\eta$ and using \eqref{E-k-mu-nullity}, we obtain the following:
\begin{align}\label{Eq-phi01}
  & 4(\nabla_{\widetilde hX} {F})(Y,Z) = (\nabla_{\widetilde QY} {F})(Z,\widetilde hX) {+}(\nabla_{\widetilde QY}{F})(\widetilde h Z,X)
   {+} (\nabla_{\widetilde QZ} {F})(\widetilde hX,Y) {+} (\nabla_{\widetilde QZ} {F})(X,\widetilde hY) \notag \\
 &-3(\nabla_{\widetilde Q\widetilde hX} {F})(Y,Z)
 -(\nabla_Y {F})(\widetilde hZ, \widetilde QX)  -(\nabla_Z {F})(\widetilde QX,\widetilde hY) \quad (X,Y,Z \in \ker\eta).
\end{align}
Taking $X,Z\in{\mathcal D}^-$ and $Y\in{\mathcal D}^+$ in \eqref{Eq-phi01}, and applying \eqref{dPhi} along with the fact $\widetilde h V= \pm \sqrt{1-\kappa}\,V$ depending on whether $V\in{\cal D}_-$ or $V\in{\cal D}_+$, we find
\begin{align}\label{Eq-N}
